subject: geography
title: UK Physical Landscapes Adventure: Glacial Processes
welcome_lead: 20,000 years ago, Britain was buried in ice. Today we read the scars it left behind.
meta_desc: GCSE Geography glaciation — corries, U-shaped valleys, moraines, Lake District.
final_note: You can identify glacial landforms in the Lake District and Snowdonia.

Armchair-shaped hollow where a glacier formed

walkthroughs.body_html:
Plucking: meltwater freezes onto rock; the glacier moves and rips the rock away.

Abrasion: rocks frozen into the ice grind the bedrock like sandpaper.

Together these create distinctive features in upland UK like the Lake District.

Corrie: round armchair hollow with steep back wall (Red Tarn, Helvellyn).

Arête: thin ridge between two corries (Striding Edge).

Pyramidal peak: pointed summit where 3+ corries meet.

U-shaped valley (glacial trough): deep, flat-floored, steep-sided.

When the glacier melts, it dumps everything it was carrying as moraine:

Terminal moraine: at the snout (end).
Lateral moraine: along the sides.
Drumlins: smooth egg-shaped hills (NW England).

options: Pyramidal peak
Arête
Drumlin
Terminal moraine

mcqs.q: Which erosion process involves the glacier freezing onto rock and tearing it away?
options: Abrasion
Plucking
Solution
Hydraulic action

mcqs.q: Why does deforestation increase flood risk?
options: Trees intercept rainfall, their roots increase infiltration and transpiration removes water — removing them increases surface runoff and reduces lag time, peaking river levels faster.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
U-shaped valleys form when rivers freeze and expand.
Deforestation causes floods because trees normally hold water in their branches forever.

mcqs.q: How do glaciers form U-shaped valleys?
options: U-shaped valleys form when rivers freeze and expand.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
Glaciers erode existing V-shaped river valleys through plucking (freezing onto rock and pulling pieces away) and abrasion (rock embedded in the ice scraping the valley floor and sides).
Glaciers carve U-shaped valleys from flat land by pushing through.
